messages:
maya: saw another latency bump on eu-west-edge last night, looks like a GPU oversubscribe pattern rather than network. stack trace/metrics attached in the alert but wanted to flag here.
opsbot: alert: gpu_node/eu-west-edge-17 high_sched_latency (90th=420ms) — possible container oversubscription. link: https://monitoring.internal/alerts/9382 :rotating_light:
sam: ugh. is this the new containerized-slicing jobs? we started allowing 2x MIG slices per pod on that fleet last week.
maya: correct, we enabled finer-grain slices to pack more tenants. but the anomaly is weird: power draw spikes followed by NVLINK errors then long scheduling delays.
devon: can you paste the pctl/log snippet? curious if it's GPU throttling or PCIe retries.
maya: here — truncated log:
```
[2026-03-19T23:12:05Z] nvidia: GPU0 perf cap reason=POWER
[2026-03-19T23:12:05Z] nvlink: lane 1 retry count=42
[2026-03-19T23:12:07Z] kubelet: container runtime pause start=230ms
[2026-03-19T23:12:08Z] scheduler: pod/candidate wait=410ms
```
lena: power cap + nvlink retries together sound like a thermal / chassis power budget issue — edge racks maybe on conservative PDUs.
sam: we should confirm if it's localized to that rack or spread across AZ. I'm going to run the probe script (lightweight) to collect per-card power, temp, nvlink errors, and MIG allocation history.
sam: running: `./tools/edge-gpu-probe --nodes eu-west-edge-{15..20} --collect=power,temp,nvlink,mig_history --out=/tmp/edgeprobe.json`
opsbot: job 54321 started by sam — ETA 90s
devon: while probe runs, can we add a short-lived metric: gpu_util_skew = max(util) - median(util) across MIG slices on same card. Oversubscribe should show high skew.
maya: good idea. we don't currently export per-slice util at that granularity to prometheus from edge agents.
ken: quick thought on mitigation: if confirmed, we can change routing policy to prefer dedicated-slice pods (no co-located tenants) for latency-sensitive customers in eu-west-edge until we reduce packing.
lena: that will increase cost though — estimate +17% egress/capacity spend for that AZ if we shift traffic.
sam: probe done, results attached: /tmp/edgeprobe.json (snippet):
```
node eu-west-edge-17: gpu0: temp=84C power=320W nvlink_retries=38 mig_slices=[a:65%, b:7%, c:6%]
node eu-west-edge-18: gpu0: temp=72C power=290W nvlink_retries=2 mig_slices=[a:40%, b:38%, c:35%]
```
devon: that pattern is classic: one tenant (slice a) hogging sustained power causing thermal/PT throttling which causes NVLINK noise and forces scheduler backoffs for other slices.
maya: tenants affected were both hosted-api customers and some dedicated traffic was also on the same rack due to a recent placement bug.
ken: placement bug? opsbot, can you show last placement shuffle for that rack?
opsbot: placement-shuffle:2026-03-19T21:00: low-priority backfill moved pods from eu-west-edge-22 -> eu-west-edge-17 to free up 22 for maintenance.
lena: so backfill packing introduced co-location of a high-throughput job with latency-sensitive slices. we should adjust backfill policy to avoid mixing latency-sensitive labels with high-throughput labels.
sam: short-term mitigation proposal: add a soft anti-affinity rule for pods with `latency-critical=true` when scheduling onto nodes with >1 active slice from different tenants.
devon: also proposermetric: emit `gpu_mig_power_pressure` per node = sum(slice_power > threshold) to trigger autoscaler action to stop extra backfills.
maya: agree. immediate actions:
- move critical tenants off eu-west-edge-17 to fallback pool (canary routing) — ken to run
- add temporary placement weight to avoid backfill into same rack — sam to patch scheduler config
- add gpu_util_skew and gpu_mig_power_pressure metrics — devon to implement collector
- create alert that fires earlier on nvlink_retries > 10 and power cap events — lena to update
ken: I'll run the move for two critical tenants now: `rbctl reroute --tenant t-28 --from node eu-west-edge-17 --to pool=edge-fallback` then monitor.
sam: patching scheduler config w/ soft anti-affinity now, will rollout to 10% of schedulers for canary.
opsbot: reroute job 54333 started by ken — ETA 40s
maya: thanks. let's sync after metric + routing changes. follow-up RFC to propose policy change for backfill mixing and cost tradeoffs.
lena: I'll draft RFC and put numbers for cost delta and SLA impact.
devon: timeline: metrics + alert today, scheduler canary tonight, full rollout if no regressions in 24h.
maya: great. please react with :thumbsup: when you’ve completed assigned tasks so we can close the incident thread.
sam: :thumbsup:
ken: :thumbsup:
devon: :thumbsup:
lena: :thumbsup:
opsbot: incident 9382 status -> mitigated (routing + metric alert)
